biosphereworlds.configuration.title: Biosphere Worlds Configuration
biosphereworlds.configuration.radius.too: Maximum radius of the spheres, in blocks (128 = default). Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.min_radius: Minimum radius of the spheres. Set it equal to the maximum radius for fixed-size spheres, or lower for per-sphere random sizing. Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.spacing.to: Distance between sphere center points on the grid, in blocks. Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.center_y.t: Y level used as the center of every sphere. Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.sphere_blo: Block ids used for the sphere shells; each sphere picks one deterministically from its grid position. On this screen you can edit, reorder or remove the existing entries, but new entries must be added to the config file by hand. Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.only_upper: Generate only the upper half of each sphere. Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.close_open: Close spheres that pass the build limit with a flat cap at the highest placeable Y (319), using the sphere shell block. Removes the natural exit at the top. Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.bedrock_mo: Bedrock at the world floor. floor: keep the bedrock_floor surface rule at the bottom of the world. none: no bedrock at the bottom, the floor is deepslate instead (the Create Diesel Generators pumpjack needs bedrock, so it will not work with this value). shell: floor plus a 3-block bedrock lining on the inside of the glass shell in the lower half of each sphere; with only_upper_hemisphere enabled it behaves exactly like floor. Only affects newly generated chunks.
biosphereworlds.configuration.generate_b: Generate bridges between adjacent spheres. Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.bridge_blo: Block id used for the bridges (for example minecraft:oak_planks). Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.bridge_rad: Radial thickness of the bridge tube; larger values make thicker bridges. Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.restrict_s: Keep structure starts inside the spheres instead of letting them generate in the void. Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.structure_: Extra inward margin, in blocks, between a structure start and the sphere edge. Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.debug_biom: Log outside-sphere biome lookup routes at DEBUG level. Diagnostic only: it does not change world generation.
biosphereworlds.configuration.edge_ocean: Flood the band next to the sphere shell with ocean: the terrain is clamped down to a flat floor so water reaches the glass. Only affects newly generated worlds.
Width of the ocean band, as a percentage of the sphere radius (0-100). Only affects newly generated worlds.
Depth of the ocean floor below sea level (63), in blocks (0-100). Only affects newly generated worlds.
biosphereworlds.configuration.satellites: Satellites

Generate small satellite spheres above each main sphere. Satellites are always complete spheres with a glass shell and a stone body. With center_y = 62 they only fit when the main radius is below roughly 200-300 blocks. Only affects newly generated worlds.
Maximum satellites per sphere
Maximum number of satellites around each main sphere (0-64). 0 disables them even when satellites_enabled is true. Only affects newly generated worlds.
Minimum satellite size
Minimum satellite radius, as a percentage of the main sphere radius (1-100, default 8). Only affects newly generated worlds.
Maximum satellite size
Maximum satellite radius, as a percentage of the main sphere radius (1-100, default 12). Only affects newly generated worlds.
Minimum satellite gap
Minimum gap between the satellite and main sphere surfaces, as a percentage of the main radius. The absolute minimum is satellites_min_gap_blocks. Only affects newly generated worlds.
Maximum satellite gap
Maximum gap between the satellite and main sphere surfaces, as a percentage of the main radius. Only affects newly generated worlds.
Minimum satellite gap in blocks
Absolute minimum gap, in blocks, between the satellite and main sphere surfaces. It is also the safety margin from the cell border and from other satellites. Only affects newly generated worlds.
Minimum satellite elevation
Minimum elevation angle of the satellites above the main sphere center, in degrees (0-90). Only affects newly generated worlds.
Maximum satellite elevation
Maximum elevation angle of the satellites above the main sphere center, in degrees (0-90). Only affects newly generated worlds.
Excluded satellite ores

Block ids or #tags that must never be chosen for a satellite core (default: ancient debris, nether quartz, nether gold and #c:ores_in_ground/deepslate). Invalid entries are ignored with a warning. Changes apply when the world is reopened or with /reload: the catalog is rebuilt only when the game tags update.
Extra satellite ores

Block ids or #tags added to the satellite core candidates even when they are not in #c:ores_in_ground/stone. Invalid entries are ignored with a warning. Changes apply when the world is reopened or with /reload: the catalog is rebuilt only when the game tags update.
Mod ore selection weight
Selection weight for ores added by other mods; vanilla ores keep their own weights. Changes apply when the world is reopened or with /reload: the catalog is rebuilt only when the game tags update.
Mod ore density (per mille)

Ore blocks per 1000 core blocks for ores added by other mods (20 = 2%). Vanilla ores keep their own densities. Changes apply when the world is reopened or with /reload: the catalog is rebuilt only when the game tags update.
